discovery: Spectroscopic detection and characterization of exoplanet atmospheres, including their molecular composition

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: The nominees turned exoplanets from points on a radial-velocity curve into physical worlds with measurable atmospheres. Seager developed the radiative-transfer theory of transmission and emission spectra that showed which atomic and molecular features could be observed. Charbonneau made the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere, sodium absorption in HD 209458b in 2002, and led pioneering transit and secondary-eclipse measurements. Tinetti's team identified water vapour in a transiting planet's atmosphere and developed the retrieval methods that are now standard. Their work rests on precise molecular physics, including line lists, cross sections and photochemistry. It opened a new observational window that JWST now exploits routinely, detecting H2O, CO2, CH4 and SO2 and even photochemical products. It links the physics of molecules and radiation directly to the question of how planets form and where the water on worlds like our own comes from.
